title: Smartwatch QT estimates show limited agreement with manual ECG readings
summary: The QT-logs study applied a trained U-Net to smartwatch ECGs and compared QTc estimates with blinded manual12-lead measurements. Among66 day-ten comparisons, mean bias was about−1 millisecond, but agreement limits extended from−46 to45 milliseconds. The selected low-risk cohort contained very few critical QTc prolongations, leaving accuracy for dangerous prolongation uncertain.
organization: Aix-Marseille University; Assistance Publique–Hôpitaux de Marseille; Cardiologs

source_review.scope: Original clinical reference/readout Methods, CNN operation/training description, paired agreement Results/Table2 and limitations; drug efficacy not assessed

evidence.ai_role: A U-Net trained on6315 annotated resting/Holter recordings identifies waveform boundaries; beat-level QTc estimates are aggregated for received smartwatch tracings. No smartwatch ECGs were used in training.
evidence.tested: Newly transmitted smartwatch ECGs were automatically analyzed in a prospective paired-measurement study. Eighty-five people entered;76 received daily follow-up. Manual12-lead reference comparisons were available for71 baseline,53 day-six and66 day-ten visits, with blinded readers.
evidence.unknown: Recordings were not consistently simultaneous and agreement was only moderate; very few critical prolongations prevented validation of clinically dangerous thresholds. Young selected participants, technical exclusions and incomplete transmissions limit transfer. No drug-safety, arrhythmia-prevention or treatment-effect conclusion is adopted. Validation3 reflects the direct paired measurement check, not independent replication or proven model-guided clinical benefit.
